speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To help me understand what you are dealing with, could you tell me how long this lesion has been present and how it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Crohn's Cutaneous Fistula (Furuncular Crohn's Disease)

I have noted your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and the prior ant bite; given your immunocompromised state from Crohn's and steroid use, we must rule out infection versus an inflammatory fistula. To differentiate these and confirm the diagnosis, please undergo a Tzanck smear, a wound culture, and an MRI of the leg to check for deep abscess formation or fistula tracking.
